B19.capture_spec: C07: scene S5 face-on square (QuadMesh 1.8 x 1.8, orthographic size 2.0 at z = 3; the square fills 90 % of the frame height and the middle 51 % of its width), lab-shaders/06-uv-colors-3d.gdshader, still PNG 3840 x 2160, Forward+. (The Lab's own quad3d fills the whole 16:9 frame: a wide rectangle, not the square the voice says.) Corner probes (0.02/0.98 of the quad): dark (0.149, 0.157, 0), red (0.992, 0.157, 0), green (0.149, 0.988, 0), yellow (0.992, 0.988, 0).
B19.visual_intent: Act title 'A Surface That Changes' (serif 40) top-left. Left: the six-line UV-colors shader with its ALBEDO line focused. Right: a real Godot render of a flat square, red across and green down. Corner labels land in the order the voice says them: 'dark' (top left), 'red' (top right), 'green' (bottom left), 'yellow' (bottom right).
B19.motion_claim: The four corner labels land on the corners in the order the voice names them.
B19.why: The picture itself is the evidence that the address became a color, and the corners prove the orientation (top left is zero, zero).

B20.visual_intent: The kit's uv_square (0 to 1 axes, the second axis pointing DOWN) at left, small. Its x axis lights up. Beneath the square a ramp strip in greys grows from the left edge (end labels '0' and '1'); a terracotta dot crosses the square from left to right and a marker rides the strip in step. Caption, GLOSSARY wording: 'ramp: a smooth run of values from 0 up to 1'. Greys only, no near-black field.
B20.motion_claim: A dot crosses the square and its x value rides the strip from 0 to 1.

show.event: ramp strip grows; marker rides; caption (the ride is done by 0.44)
strip stays as the base of the next beats

B20.why: The ramp is the series' signature object; a marker riding a strip as a dot crosses the square ties 'x' to 'a smooth run' in one motion.

B21.visual_intent: Three stacked strips on the cream stage: 'x' (the ramp, 0 to 1, greys), 'x × 8' (the same strip relabelled 0 to 8 with eight tick marks) and 'fract(x × 8)' drawn as a sawtooth plot with eight teeth, settled by 0.45, with a terracotta dot waiting at its start until 0.56 and then travelling along it, snapping back to zero at every whole number; under the plot, a strip of eight repeated grey ramps. Caption, GLOSSARY wording: 'fract(x): the part after the point: x minus floor(x)', and under it the one-line gloss of the word it uses, GLOSSARY wording: 'floor(x): rounds down to the whole number below'. Double the space at the fused boundary of 'x × 8' and look at the still.
B21.motion_claim: The strip stretches to eight, then the dot traces a sawtooth with eight teeth.

show.event: sawtooth plot draws in (settled by 0.45), the dot waits at its start; captions
the dot travels along the sawtooth, snapping back to zero eight times (as the voice says 'starts over at zero at every whole number')

B21.why: Stretch, then restart at every whole number, is a transformation of one strip into another; the sawtooth with a travelling dot shows it.

B22.visual_intent: The sawtooth plot (eight teeth) with a horizontal threshold line at 0.5. Under it the output plot of step(0.5, ·): a square wave with eight high and eight low segments. A terracotta dot travels along the sawtooth; each time it crosses the threshold the lower plot flips and a small spark flashes. At the bottom, a strip in two greys (light and dark stripes) fills in as the dot passes. Caption (docs wording): 'step(edge, x): 0 below the edge, 1 from the edge up'.
B22.motion_claim: Every time the dot crosses the threshold the lower plot flips and a stripe appears.

show.event: dot travels; flips; stripe strip fills

B22.why: A threshold crossing that flips an output is the definition of step; the dot makes each crossing visible.

cues.label: step(edge, x): 0 below the edge, 1 from the edge up
fract(x): the part after the point: x minus floor(x)

B24.visual_intent: Two strips: 't' (0 to 1) above, and 'mix(a, b, t)' below running from a = 0.2 to b = 0.8, each with a terracotta dot. The dot on t slides from 0 to 1 and the dot below slides from 0.2 to 0.8 in step; the end values 0.2 and 0.8 are labelled. Caption from the first frame, GLOSSARY wording: 'mix(a, b, t): blends from a to b: t of 0 gives a, 1 gives b'; a formula caption lands with the voice's 'Mix of a': 'a × (1 − t) + b × t'. Greys only. It is plain numbers on purpose: no colors, so no renderer is implied.
B24.motion_claim: The two dots slide together: t from 0 to 1, the blend from a to b.

show.event: t dot slides; blend dot follows from 0.2 to 0.8 (the slide is done by 0.44)

B24.why: A weight sliding from 0 to 1 with a value sliding from a to b is mix in motion; the formula is the caption, not the picture.

props.title: Hints: how Godot treats a uniform
rows: keep this dial between 0 and 1, in the editor
props.note: hint: the word after a colon that tells Godot how to treat a uniform · Godot 4.7 shading language reference

B26.visual_intent: A two-row table pairing each hint with what it tells Godot; the table's note line carries the GLOSSARY definition word for word: 'hint: the word after a colon that tells Godot how to treat a uniform', then the docs page. Each row lands on its words.
B26.motion_claim: Each row lands and is ringed on its words.
B26.why: Two facts in two rows; no editor frame was recorded for this film, and the table claims only what the docs say (a hint tells Godot how to treat a uniform; a range hint shapes the editor), not how a widget looks.
